This variant is classified as a variant of unknown significance because its contribution to mitochondrial developmental encephalopathy with optic neuropathy has not been confirmed.

In 2 first cousins from a consanguineous family with mitochondrial developmental encephalopathy with optic neuropathy, Marco-Hernandez et al. (2022) identified homozygosity for a c.895A-G transition (c.895A-G, NM_006839) in the IMMT gene, resulting in a lys299-to-glu (K299D) substitution at a conserved residue. The mutation, which was identified by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, segregated with disease in the family and was found only once in the gnomAD database with an allele frequency of 0.0000046. Mitochondrial morphology was abnormal in muscle tissue from both patients, but further functional studies were not performed. Patient 1, a 10-year-old boy, presented with nystagmus from birth. An ophthalmologic examination demonstrated bilateral torsional nystagmus with bilateral optic atrophy. At 3 years of age he had developmental delay and absence of language, and on examination he had action tremor, nystagmus, and stereotypies. He developed partial seizures at 4 years of age. Brain MRI showed abnormal signal in the bilateral globus pallidus. Muscle biopsy showed normal respiratory chain activity but abnormal-appearing mitochondria. Patient 2, a 12-year-old boy, had developmental delay and nystagmus noted in the first months of life. On examination, he had nystagmus, moderately impaired intellectual development, autism spectrum disorder, tremor, dysmetria, and microcephaly.
